name: Sports trivia (easy)
description: 50 easy questions about rules, famous athletes, events and records that no longer change. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: How long is an official marathon?
items.explain: All official marathons are 26.2 miles (42.195 km), a distance standardized in the early 20th century.

items.question: In which city was the first organized marathon run at the 1896 Games, the start of the modern Olympic era?
items.explain: The first organized marathon was run in Athens at the 1896 Olympics, the first Games of the modern era.

items.question: The marathon commemorates a legendary run to bring news of an Athenian victory over which enemy?
items.explain: The legend says a Greek soldier ran from Marathon to Athens in 490 BCE to announce the victory over the Persians.

items.question: The 1908 Olympic marathon, which gave us today's standard distance, started at which royal residence?
items.explain: The British Olympic Committee started the 1908 race at Windsor Castle and finished it in front of the royal box in the London stadium, which produced the 26.2-mile distance.

items.question: Who invented the game of basketball in 1891?
items.explain: James Naismith, a physical education instructor in Springfield, Massachusetts, invented basketball in 1891.

items.question: What were the goals in the very first games of basketball?
items.explain: Naismith started out using 10-foot-high peach baskets as the goals for each team.

items.question: In which country was basketball's inventor, James Naismith, born?
items.explain: Naismith was born in Almonte, Ontario, Canada, in 1861.

items.question: In 1947, Jackie Robinson broke Major League Baseball's color barrier playing for which team?
items.explain: Robinson took the field for the Brooklyn Dodgers on April 15, 1947, ending the decades-old color line in MLB.

items.question: Which jersey number is worn by every MLB player on Jackie Robinson Day each April 15?
items.explain: April 15 is observed throughout MLB with players wearing Robinson's former Dodgers number, 42.

items.question: Which award did Jackie Robinson win in 1947, his first season in the majors?
items.explain: Robinson took home the Rookie of the Year Award in 1947, and later won the MVP Award in 1949.

items.question: In 1976, Nadia Comăneci became the first Olympian to score a perfect 10 in which sport?
items.explain: Comăneci was the first gymnast to be awarded a perfect 10 in an Olympic event, at the Montreal Games.

items.question: How old was Nadia Comăneci when she scored her first perfect 10 at the 1976 Olympics?
items.explain: She was only 14 when she scored the first perfect 10 on the uneven bars on July 18, 1976.

source.title: This week in Olympic history July 15-21: Nadia Comaneci scores the first perfect 10 in gymnastics

items.question: How many perfect 10s did Nadia Comăneci score at the 1976 Montreal Olympics?
items.explain: She received seven perfect scores in Montreal and won three gold medals there.

items.question: How many gold medals did Jesse Owens win at the 1936 Berlin Olympics?
items.explain: Owens won gold in the long jump, the 100 m, the 200 m and the 4 x 100 m relay.

items.question: Which of these events did Jesse Owens NOT win gold in at the 1936 Olympics?
items.explain: Owens won the long jump, the 100 m, the 200 m and the 4 x 100 m relay, but not the hurdles.

items.question: Which American sprinter matched Jesse Owens' four track-and-field golds at a single Games in 1984?
items.explain: Owens' feat stood alone until Carl Lewis matched it at the 1984 Olympics.

source.title: How Jesse Owens Foiled Hitler's Plans for the 1936 Olympics

items.question: Who became the first athlete to run a mile in under four minutes?
items.explain: Roger Bannister ran 3 minutes 59.4 seconds in a meet at Oxford.

items.question: In which year did the first sub-four-minute mile take place?
items.explain: Bannister broke the four-minute barrier on May 6, 1954.

items.question: In which English university city did Roger Bannister run his historic four-minute mile?
items.explain: He ran it at the Iffley Road track in Oxford, during a meet between the Amateur Athletic Association and Oxford University.

source.title: Roger Bannister runs first four-minute mile

items.question: In the 1974 "Rumble in the Jungle," Muhammad Ali knocked out which heavyweight champion?
items.explain: Ali beat champion George Foreman by knockout in Kinshasa on October 30, 1974.

items.question: In which African city was the "Rumble in the Jungle" fought?
items.explain: The fight took place in Kinshasa, in what was then Zaire and is now the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

items.question: What was the name of the strategy Ali used against Foreman, leaning on the ropes to let his opponent tire?
items.explain: Ali leaned against the ropes and let Foreman throw punches and exhaust himself, a tactic known as the rope-a-dope.

items.question: In which round did Muhammad Ali knock out George Foreman in 1974?
items.explain: Ali won by knockout in the eighth round.

items.question: How many FIFA World Cups did Pelé win, a feat no other player has achieved?
items.explain: Pelé won the World Cup in 1958, 1962 and 1970, and he is the only player to have won it three times.

items.question: Which national team did Pelé lead to three World Cup titles?
items.explain: Pelé was part of the Brazilian teams that won the World Cup in 1958, 1962 and 1970.

items.question: How old was Pelé when he won his first World Cup in 1958, making him the youngest winner ever?
items.explain: Pelé won the 1958 World Cup at just 17 years old, the youngest player to win the tournament.

items.question: Pelé was nicknamed "O Rei" after the 1958 World Cup. What does this mean in English?
items.explain: "O Rei" is Portuguese for "the King", a nickname Pelé earned after the 1958 World Cup.

items.question: Which jersey number was retired across the entire NHL in honor of Wayne Gretzky?
items.explain: The NHL retired Gretzky's number 99 league-wide, so no player can wear it again.

items.question: What was Wayne Gretzky's famous nickname?
items.explain: Gretzky was nicknamed "the Great One" for his achievements in the NHL.

items.question: Gretzky led which team to four Stanley Cup championships in the 1980s?
items.explain: As center and team captain, Gretzky led the Edmonton Oilers to four Stanley Cup titles.

items.question: How many interlocking rings make up the Olympic symbol?
items.explain: The symbol has five interlaced rings, which Pierre de Coubertin said represent the five parts of the world.

source.title: Who created the Olympic rings symbol?

items.question: Who created the Olympic rings symbol in 1913?
items.explain: The rings first appeared in 1913 on a letter by Pierre de Coubertin, founder of the modern Olympic Games.

source.title: Who created the Olympic rings symbol?

items.question: The Olympic motto "Citius, Altius, Fortius" is Latin for what?
items.explain: The Latin motto, proposed by Pierre de Coubertin, translates as "Faster, Higher, Stronger".

items.question: Which colour is NOT one of the five Olympic ring colours?
items.explain: The rings are blue, yellow, black, green and red on a white background, with no purple.

source.title: The Power of the Rings - Olympic News

items.question: Wimbledon is the only Grand Slam tennis tournament still played on which surface?
items.explain: Of the four Grand Slams, only Wimbledon is still played on grass, which is where the name "lawn tennis" comes from.

items.question: In which year was the first Wimbledon championship held, making it the world's oldest tennis tournament?
items.explain: The first Wimbledon was held in 1877, with a single event, the Gentleman's Singles.

items.question: Which Grand Slam tennis tournament is played on clay?
items.explain: The Australian and US Opens are played on hard courts and the French Open is played on clay.

items.question: What is the maximum break, a perfect clearance, in a standard frame of snooker?
items.explain: A maximum break is 147: all 15 reds each followed by the black, then all six colours.

items.question: How many red balls are racked at the start of a full frame of snooker?
items.explain: A full frame starts with 15 reds, which is why a maximum break involves potting 15 reds with 15 blacks.

items.question: Which player passed Babe Ruth's career total of 714 home runs in 1974?
items.explain: Ruth's 714 home runs stood as the record until Hank Aaron surpassed it in 1974.

source.title: Babe Ruth: The Sultan of Swat and his Williamsport legacy

items.question: Which team did Babe Ruth begin his major league career with, as a star left-handed pitcher?
items.explain: Ruth started as a pitcher for the Boston Red Sox before becoming a slugging outfielder for the Yankees.

items.question: Which nickname did sportswriters give Babe Ruth?
items.explain: Sportswriters nicknamed Ruth the "Sultan of Swat" while he was an outfielder for the New York Yankees.

items.question: How many home runs did Babe Ruth hit in 1927, a single-season record that stood until 1961?
items.explain: Ruth hit 60 home runs in 1927, a record that stood until 1961.

items.question: How many points did Wilt Chamberlain score in a single NBA game on March 2, 1962?
items.explain: Chamberlain scored 100 points for the Philadelphia Warriors in a 169-147 win, an NBA single-game record.

items.question: Which team did Wilt Chamberlain's Warriors beat in his 100-point game?
items.explain: The Philadelphia Warriors beat the New York Knicks 169-147 on the night Chamberlain scored 100.

items.question: In which Pennsylvania town was Wilt Chamberlain's 100-point game played?
items.explain: The game was held in a small arena in Hershey, Pennsylvania, and was not televised.

items.question: In 1980, the "Miracle on Ice" saw the US men's hockey team upset which heavily favored opponent?
items.explain: A team of American college players beat the defending four-time gold-medal-winning Soviet Union at the Lake Placid Games.

items.question: In which New York town were the 1980 Winter Olympics, home of the "Miracle on Ice," held?
items.explain: The Miracle on Ice game was played at the Lake Placid 1980 Olympic Winter Games.

items.question: What was the final score of the "Miracle on Ice" game between the United States and the Soviet Union?
items.explain: The United States beat the Soviet Union 4-3 on February 22, 1980, then won the gold medal by beating Finland.

items.question: Who coached the US hockey team to its "Miracle on Ice" win over the Soviets in 1980?
items.explain: The Miracle on Ice team of college players was coached by Herb Brooks.

source.title: When the US Olympic Hockey Team Stunned the World
